note: Seed for SNPCurate: the 21 entries of Table 4 in benchmark_section_draft.md. Evidence tiers are proposed, not curated.

entries.label: N6K (Lys6 in teosinte, Asn6 in maize)

refs.cite: Wang H, et al. 2015. Genetics 200:965-974
Fairbanks RA, Ross-Ibarra J. 2025. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 122:e2503748122

entries.note: The only fixed difference in tga1 between teosinte and maize. The alternate allele is the teosinte lysine; B73 carries the maize asparagine.

entries.label: T344N

refs.cite: Fu Z, et al. 2013. Theor Appl Genet 126:923-935
Palaisa KA, et al. 2003. Plant Cell 15:1795-1806

entries.note: Thr to Asn in exon 5 of phytoene synthase, associated with total carotenoid content. Not required for yellow kernels: B73 is yellow and carries the reference threonine.

entries.label: Phe469 insertion (high-oil allele)

refs.cite: Zheng P, et al. 2008. Nat Genet 40:367-372

entries.note: A phenylalanine insertion that raises oil and oleic acid. In-frame insertions have no language-model score.

entries.label: Exon 1 missense D70E
entries.trait: Provitamin A, ratio of alpha to beta branch carotenoids

refs.cite: Harjes CE, et al. 2008. Science 319:330-333

entries.note: The one missense change in exon 1. Its association with orange kernels in this set follows tropical ancestry.
entries.needs_review: Is this the SNP216 of Harjes et al.? Confirm against the published sequence.

entries.label: E214G
entries.trait: Banded leaf and sheath blight resistance

refs.cite: Li N, et al. 2019. Nat Genet 51:1540-1548

entries.note: One of two linked substitutions homozygous in about 710 lines. GRIN holds no descriptor for the disease.
entries.needs_review: Confirm that E214G and S217R are the two substitutions reported for the resistant allele.

entries.label: S217R
entries.trait: Banded leaf and sheath blight resistance

refs.cite: Li N, et al. 2019. Nat Genet 51:1540-1548

entries.note: Travels with E214G.
entries.needs_review: Confirm that E214G and S217R are the two substitutions reported for the resistant allele.

entries.label: F163L (second change of su1-ref)

refs.cite: Dinges JR, et al. 2001. Plant Physiol 125:1406-1418

entries.note: Present on the su1-ref allele with W578R, which is not a site. Homozygous in all 11 lines whose GRIN kernel type is sweet and in 102 other lines, so it does not identify sweet corn by itself.

entries.label: Promoter variant about 1.1 kb upstream (rare, late)

refs.cite: Guo L, et al. 2018. Curr Biol 28:3005-3015

entries.note: Rare group found in 4 of 7 teosinte lines and 20 of 86 tropical lines; carriers silk later. 1,097 bp upstream of the start codon in B73 v5.
entries.needs_review: Is this SNP-1245 of Guo et al.? Their flanking sequence settles it.

entries.label: Promoter indel about 2.5 kb upstream (common, early)

refs.cite: Guo L, et al. 2018. Curr Biol 28:3005-3015

entries.note: Common group, homozygous in half of the lines, associated with earlier silking. 2,532 bp upstream of the start codon in B73 v5.
entries.needs_review: Is this the upstream block (Indel-2339) of Guo et al.? Confirm.

entries.label: W578R (su1-ref)

refs.cite: Dinges JR, et al. 2001. Plant Physiol 125:1406-1418

entries.note: The causal change of the su1-ref allele. No site in codon 578 in this release.

entries.label: Ser220Asn

refs.cite: Liu L, et al. 2015. PLoS Genet 11:e1005670

entries.note: Codon 220, base 2. The one significant marker inside ub3 in the NAM ear row number scan, and not a site in this release.

entries.label: Start codon change (natural knockout, Oh43 type)

refs.cite: Handrick V, et al. 2016. Plant Cell 28:1682-1700

entries.note: The start-codon site is not in this release. The haplotype is recovered by SC0017.

entries.label: Splice-site variant

refs.cite: Zhang X, et al. 2019. Nat Commun 10:5608

entries.note: The published variant (G/GT to C/GT) is at the 5' splice site of an intron in the 5' UTR. The B73 v5 gene model has a single exon, so no splice consequence can be annotated, and none of the 12 sites in that region (chr7:6,008,413-6,008,669) matches the change. By GRIN kernel type, missense T166A (chr7:6,007,879) is homozygous in 12 of the 24 lines recorded as sweet or pop and in 94 of the 835 field-type lines (dent, semident, semiflint or flint), and a haplotype of six sites just past the 3' end of the gene (chr7:6,007,105-6,007,322; counted at its last site) in 19 of 24 against 140 of 835. That is not evidence for the gene: 2,241 of the 21,246 other 100-kb windows of the genome hold a usable site that separates sweet or pop lines from field types more strongly than any in the window around tin1.

entries.label: 5' transposon, InDel4 and 3' transposon alleles

refs.cite: Yan J, et al. 2010. Nat Genet 42:322-327

entries.note: The favorable alleles are transposon and indel haplotypes, not sites. An 18 bp in-frame insertion (380 lines) and a stop-gained variant (10 lines) are present instead.

entries.label: Extracellular-domain allelic series

refs.cite: Hurni S, et al. 2015. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 112:8780-8785
Yang P, et al. 2021. Plant J 106:526-535

entries.note: Most missense sites in the gene have more heterozygous than homozygous carriers, the signature of reads from related kinase genes.

entries.label: Coding and promoter variants

refs.cite: Yang Q, et al. 2017. Nat Genet 49:1364-1372

entries.note: The gene model is absent from the annotation behind the consequence calls, so the sites inside it are annotated only as upstream of a neighbor.

entries.label: Tag of the Oh43-type knockout haplotype

refs.cite: Handrick V, et al. 2016. Plant Cell 28:1682-1700

entries.note: Carried by Oh43 and lines descended from it. Annotated as a frameshift, but it is one half of a 9 bp in-frame insertion whose other half is not a site.

entries.label: Tag of the White Cap haplotype

refs.cite: Tan BC, et al. 2017. Genetics 206:135-150

entries.note: The causal change is a tandem array of Ccd1 copies. This site, 616 bp from wc1, is homozygous in 58 of 97 white-kernel lines.

entries.label: Lead SNP for pericarp and cob pigment

refs.cite: Schoemaker DL, et al. 2024. G3 14:jkad256

entries.note: The strongest association for pericarp pigmentation in the Wisconsin Diversity panel, and homozygous in 335 of 346 white-cob lines here. It lies in the paralog p2, 24 kb from the p1 repeat cluster.

entries.label: Tag of the sulfonylurea-susceptible haplotype

refs.cite: Zhang Y, et al. 2024. Front Plant Sci 15:1443413
Nordby JN, et al. 2008. Weed Sci 56:376-382

entries.note: Homozygous in 16 of 19 susceptible and 4 of 32 tolerant lines. It lies 14 kb from CYP81A9 in the neighboring P450 gene; no coding variant inside CYP81A9 separates the groups.

entries.label: Lead NAM SNP of the photoperiod peak

refs.cite: Hung HY, et al. 2012. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 109:E1913-E1921
Yang Q, et al. 2013. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 110:16969-16974
Wang C, et al. 2017. New Phytol 215:1503-1515
Tibbs-Cortes LE, et al. 2024. Genome Res 34:1253-1263

entries.note: The causal variant is a transposon in the promoter. This marker, 40 kb from the gene, is homozygous in 14 of 86 tropical lines and no Stiff Stalk, Non-Stiff Stalk or Iodent line.
